sourceChecks.title: Senolytics decrease senescent cells in humans: Preliminary report from a clinical trial of Dasatinib plus Quercetin in individuals with diabetic kidney disease
sourceChecks.excerpt: D + Q reduced adipose tissue senescent cell burden within 11 days
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Phase 1 open-label study of nine people with diabetic kidney disease reported reduced senescence markers in adipose and skin after dasatinib plus quercetin.
sourceChecks.limitations: Narrow short-term tissue-marker outcome, not complete/selective clearance of all senescent cells throughout the body or long-term safety. Independent review reopened and read original source snapshot; live availability not asserted.

sourceChecks.title: Reprogramming to recover youthful epigenetic information and restore vision
sourceChecks.excerpt: restores youthful DNA methylation patterns and transcriptomes
sourceChecks.paraphrase: OSK expression in mouse retinal ganglion cells restored selected youthful methylation/transcriptome features and improved regeneration/vision in injury, glaucoma and old-mouse settings.
sourceChecks.limitations: Mouse retinal cells and tissues only; does not show safe systemic whole-body reprogramming or human-scale rejuvenation. Independent review reopened and read original source snapshot; live availability not asserted.

sourceChecks.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice
sourceChecks.excerpt: dietary encapsulated rapamycin increases mouse survival
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Multisite study found late-life rapamycin extended median and maximum survival in genetically heterogeneous mice of both sexes.
sourceChecks.limitations: No safe single-agent human longevity result, no 50% healthy-lifespan extension, and survival may involve cancer delay and strain/context effects. Independent review reopened and read original source snapshot; live availability not asserted.

items.corrections: A mouse retinal reprogramming study improved age-associated vision and selected molecular-age features, a narrow intervention result relevant to rejuvenation. Does not show safe systemic reversal of all hallmarks in adult humans.

A targeted search found a review specifically discussing causal aging drivers, but its inspected PubMed page was unreadable. The exact single primary driver remains unassessed from readable source material; no consensus claim is made.
A small human phase 1 study reported reduction of tissue senescence markers after dasatinib plus quercetin. Does not establish complete, safe, selective clearance of all senescent cells in vivo.

A relevant mouse GDF11 paper was found, but the actual opened PubMed page was unreadable in this retrieval. Search-result text is not used to substantiate rejuvenation; no full organism or human effect assessed.

OSK altered selected epigenetic signatures and function in mouse retinal cells, including old-mouse vision outcomes. This is tissue-specific mouse evidence, not complete safe systemic reprogramming to a youthful state.

A bounded search did not locate a primary result establishing a unified theory/intervention for negligible senescence. Universal mechanism and safe transferable intervention remain unsupported by the inspected material.

The targeted GDF11 muscle paper is directly relevant to aged muscle stem cells but the opened page was unreadable. The claimed master regulator across all tissues cannot be assessed from accessible primary evidence here.
A relevant aged-mouse trehalose/proteostasis paper was found, but the actual PMC page was blocked. No complete mechanism or safe reversal of organism-wide proteostasis collapse can be assessed.

A relevant multi-omics aging biomarker paper was found, but its inspected full text page was blocked. The asserted predictive true biological age and remaining-healthspan panel is not verified; search snippets are excluded.
Multisite experiments showed late-life rapamycin extended median and maximum lifespan in mice. No safe single drug result shows 50% or greater healthy-lifespan extension across mammals or people.

notes: All three positively used primary source URLs independently reopened; title/topic/excerpt/result scope match.

Retained partial classifications for nine-person open-label senolytic marker study, mouse retinal OSK intervention and mouse rapamycin survival. No human systemic rejuvenation or >=50% healthy-lifespan inference.
Five inaccessible outcomes and one bounded unsupported outcome remain truth-neutral; no source failure treated as scientific disproof.
